purpose: Tiotropium is used to help people breathe more easily when they have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), which includes conditions like emphysema and chronic bronchitis. It can also help control asthma in some patients. It is a maintenance medication, meaning you use it every day to keep your airways open and prevent breathing problems.
how_it_works: Your airways can tighten up and make it hard to breathe due to COPD or asthma. Tiotropium works by blocking signals in your lungs that cause the airway muscles to squeeze. This helps the muscles relax, which opens up your airways and makes it easier to breathe all day long.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth is the most common side effect. You may also notice a dry or irritated throat, constipation, blurred vision, or difficulty urinating. Some people get a mild cough after using the inhaler.
warnings: This medication is NOT a rescue inhaler — do not use it for sudden breathing attacks. If you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, or trouble urinating, tell your doctor before using this. Avoid getting the mist or powder in your eyes, as it can worsen glaucoma. Seek emergency help if your breathing suddenly gets worse after using it.
typical_dosing: You inhale Tiotropium once a day, every day at the same time. With the HandiHaler device, you use one capsule per day. With the Respimat inhaler, you take two puffs once a day. Never swallow the capsules — they are only meant to be inhaled through the device.
